summary: The book stood pat on 11-18: no trades, P1 (sell half of VTI) rejected, and four thesis_updates. I still think the reasoning was sound. The tradeoffs were stated and the Skeptic's and Implicator's points were checked against the lot data. P1's 'VTI lags SPY' thesis ran against the 21-day numbers. Its tax claim was wrong: about $0.71 of the loss would have been wash-sale disallowed against the 11-16 lot. I was also right that a VOO sale would not have harvested cleanly, because the 10-23 and 10-26 lots fall within 30 days. On the day VTI fell 0.26% and VOO 0.29%, which matches the Skeptic's 21-day read, though one day is not evidence. Equity rose $0.46 to $621.35 while the SPY benchmark fell about 0.3%. Since v6 the account is -0.19%, against -1.73% for the shadow and -2.63% for SPY. The low-beta tilt is doing what it was built to do, and that is the design working, not a grade. The open risk is bigger than at the open. SPY closed at 730.20, only 0.06% above the stored 729.79 line, so VOO and VTI (about 23.3% of equity) are one tick from the shared stop. The stored line is the 11-17 figure, and the moving 200-day may already sit at or above today's close. MCO is NEAR, 2.4% above $470, after I restated its thesis and named it the first sell candidate. The restated thesis keeps a position whose original reason is gone, and the only exit is its stop, since I cannot originate a sale. All the L6 fixes stuck in close.json: SAM's stop restated from its $220.14 fill, the SPY line re-dated to 729.79, MCO's role restated. No price stop tripped. EXEL (5.1% above its stop) and INCY (7.1%) are the closest single names after MCO. The cash call (11.5%, about $9 over the buffer) cited the WMT print, the 16.5% Staples bucket and the risk-off stance rather than L4. That is defensible for one more session. The 11-13 commitment to deploy after 11-19 now comes due, and Staples and Health Care, the Market Analyst's favored buckets, are already the most crowded.

broken_theses.why: The original premise, 'Financials is a Market Analyst favored sector', broke on 11-18: he now favors only Staples, Health Care and Utilities, and the exposure packet buckets MCO as Industrials, which he avoids. I restated the thesis on quality and low beta under L8 rather than defend the old role, which was right. But the restated version is a hold by default: no tilt supports it, rising long yields and soft IG credit (LQD 2.41% and HYG 1.10% below their 200-days) are named headwinds, and it closed at $481.29, NEAR at 2.4% above the $470 stop. The price clause has not tripped, so this is a broken premise, not a tripped invalidation. The next run should either get a sell proposal or say explicitly why the stop alone is the plan.

lessons: A moving-average stop stored as a fixed number goes stale every session. With SPY 0.06% above a line dated 11-17, the stop block's 'near' status may already be wrong. Before trusting the status, re-date the SPY 200-day from the Market Analyst's latest SMA and check regime_allows_buys, because the regime filter computes today's line, not the stored one.

Rejecting a partial trim because 'the stored stop is the plan' holds only if the stop is actually executed when it trips. I can approve or shrink proposals but cannot originate a sale. When a shared stop is within about 0.5%, the next decision should state that a tripped SPY 200-day means selling all of VOO and VTI together (the 11-17 pre-commitment), and the Proposer should be asked to put that sale up the same day it trips, not argue it again.

Naming a holding 'first sell candidate' has no effect if no proposal follows. For MCO, the Proposer's next holdings_review should give a sell-or-hold verdict on the restated quality/low-beta thesis, and the PM should judge it then instead of leaving the decision to the $470 close.

Soft clauses in stored theses need a verdict when their condition is met. FAST's text says it is 'a marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging', and XLI is 4.66% below its 200-day. On 11-18 I accepted the hold on low beta without saying whether that condition had been met. Either restate FAST's role through thesis_updates or name it with MCO as a trim candidate (L8).

The post-11-19 deployment commitment has to be sized against buckets, not cash. Staples is 16.5% and Health Care 12.8%, and L3's evidence shows these names fall together. If WMT's print is clean, ask for a named candidate with its own stop. Prefer one outside those two buckets that the Market Analyst does not avoid, so the invested gap to the shadow closes without stacking more of the same factor.
